question: In what year did Rust reach its first stable release, 1.0?

subquestions: What year was Rust 1.0 released (the first stable release)?

observations.content:
Summary: Rust 1.0, the first stable release, was published on May 15, 2015. The language has since grown in popularity and adoption. The latest version as of 2026 is 1.91.0.

[1] Rust (programming language)
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)
    Six years after Mozilla's sponsorship, Rust 1.0 was published and became the first stable release on May 15, 2015. A year later, the Rust compiler had accumulated over 1,400 contributors, and there were over 5,000 third-party libraries published on the Rust package management website Crates.io.: 43:15

### 2015–2020: Servo and early adoption

[edit&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2015–2020: Servo and early adoption")] [...] Software developer Graydon Hoare created Rust in 2006 while working at Mozilla, which officially sponsored the project in 2009. The first stable release, Rust 1.0, was published in May 2015. The project has been sponsored by the Rust Foundation since February 2021.

Rust has been adopted by many software projects, especially web services and system software. It has been studied academically and has a growing community of developers.

## History [...] During this time period, work had shifted from the initial OCaml compiler to a self-hosting compiler (i.e., written in Rust) targeting LLVM. The ownership system was in place by 2010. The Rust logo was developed in 2011 based on a bicycle chainring.

Rust 0.1 became the first public release on January 20, 2012 for Windows, Linux, and MacOS. The early 2010s witnessed increasing involvement from full-time engineers at Mozilla and open source volunteers outside Mozilla.

Background

The Rust programming language emerged in 2006 as a personal project by Mozilla employee Graydon Hoare, with Mozilla beginning to sponsor the project in 2009. The first version-numbered Rust compiler was released in January 2012. Rust 1.0, the first stable version, was released on May 15, 2015.

6 [...] "Rust" was initially a personal project by Graydon Hoare of Mozilla. In 2009, Mozilla began sponsoring the project, with several Mozilla employees participating in the design and development of the Rust language. In August 2013, Graydon Hoare stepped down from his role as technical lead for Rust, and Brian Anderson took over. On May 15, 2015, the Rust 1.0 version was officially released.     https://medium.com/@mattdark/rust-a-systems-programming-language-272ca761dfa0
    ## About

Rust is a systems programming language developed by the engineers of Mozilla. Rust could be categorized as a new language, as Rust 1.0, the first stable version was released on May 15th, 2015. The latest version today is Rust 1.20, that was released on August 31st, this year.

Rust is a compiled language like C or C++.
